title: Ravindra Jadeja Scripts History With 350th Test Wicket in Galle
excerpt: The Indian all-rounder became only the fourth cricketer in history to score 4,000 runs and take 350 wickets in Test cricket, joining Kapil Dev, Ian Botham, and Daniel Vettori in an elite club — and he did it in fewer than 100 matches.
body:
• Ravindra Jadeja became the fourth cricketer in history to score 4,000+ runs and take 350+ wickets in Test cricket
  • He joins Kapil Dev (5,248 runs, 434 wickets), Ian Botham (5,200 runs, 383 wickets), and Daniel Vettori (4,531 runs, 362 wickets) in the elite club
  • Jadeja reached the milestone on Day 3 of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with 4,108 runs and 350 wickets in just 90 Tests
  • He is the only member of this quartet to achieve the double before playing 100 Test matches

Ravindra Jadeja reached a historic milestone on the third day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle on Monday, becoming only the fourth cricketer in Test history to score at least 4,000 runs and take 350 or more wickets in the longest format, according to the Times of India.

The 36-year-old left-arm spinner picked up his second wicket of the innings when Sri Lanka's Keshara Nuwantha attempted to slap-drive an away-turner through the off side. The ball took a deflection off his knee and ballooned towards Shubman Gill, who completed the catch to seal the record, according to the Times of India.

An Elite Club of Four

Jadeja's achievement places him alongside three legendary all-rounders who have managed the same rare double:

https://x.com/imvikaskohli/status/2089313013929304475

Kapil Dev (India) — 5,248 runs and 434 wickets in 131 Tests
Ian Botham (England) — 5,200 runs and 383 wickets in 102 Tests
Daniel Vettori (New Zealand) — 4,531 runs and 362 wickets in 113 Tests
Ravindra Jadeja (India) — 4,108 runs and 350 wickets in 90 Tests

What sets Jadeja apart is efficiency. He is the only member of this quartet to reach the milestone in fewer than 100 Test matches. Botham was the previous fastest, achieving the double in his 72nd Test, but at the lower threshold of 4,000 runs and 300 wickets. At the 350-wicket mark, Jadeja stands alone in speed, according to the Times of India.

First Indian Spin All-Rounder

While Kapil Dev achieved the runs-and-wickets double as a fast-bowling all-rounder, Jadeja is the first Indian spinner to reach this landmark, according to CricToday. The distinction matters because left-arm spin operates under fundamentally different demands than pace bowling — requiring sustained accuracy, surface reading, and the ability to extract turn across varying conditions.

Jadeja is now the fifth Indian to reach 350 Test wickets overall, joining Anil Kumble (619), Ravichandran Ashwin (537), Kapil Dev (434), and Harbhajan Singh (417), according to the Times of India.

Among left-arm spinners in Test history, he trails only Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath (433) and Vettori (362) in total wickets.

"Jadeja's all-round contribution has repeatedly allowed India to balance their playing XI."

— Times of India

The Journey to This Point

Jadeja's path to this record was far from straightforward. He made his Test debut against England in 2012 but struggled to cement his place in the squad during his early years and was dropped on multiple occasions, according to TrendKia.

His comeback during the 2015-16 season proved decisive. Since then, he has become indispensable to India's red-ball setup, contributing six Test centuries and 28 half-centuries with the bat, alongside 15 five-wicket hauls and three 10-wicket match hauls with the ball, according to CricToday.

In domestic cricket, his batting prowess is underscored by three triple centuries in the Ranji Trophy. He was also part of India's victorious T20 World Cup squad in 2024, after which he retired from the shortest format.

Jadeja missed the one-off Test against Afghanistan earlier this year due to an injury sustained during IPL 2026, making his return to the Test squad in Galle all the more significant, according to CricToday.

Match Context

India posted 462 in their first innings in Galle, with Jadeja contributing 13 runs. Sri Lanka were 243 for 7 in reply when Jadeja's milestone wicket fell. The first Test remained in progress at the time of the milestone, with India firmly in control.

What's Next

With the second Test of the series still to come, Jadeja has the opportunity to add to both his wicket and run tallies and further cement his position among Test cricket's greatest all-rounders. For Indian cricket fans across the diaspora — from watch parties in New Jersey to early-morning streams in the Bay Area — Jadeja's record is another chapter in the sport's enduring hold on the community's imagination.
